content.title: Why Dynamic Programming?
content.description: Dynamic Programming (DP) helps solve complex problems by breaking them into smaller overlapping subproblems and storing previously computed results.

content.content: Many recursive solutions repeatedly solve the same subproblems. Dynamic Programming eliminates this redundancy by storing intermediate results, dramatically improving performance.

content.title: Real-World Applications
content.content: Route optimization, resource allocation, stock trading, AI decision making, scheduling systems, and sequence analysis all use Dynamic Programming.
What is Dynamic Programming?

content.definition: An optimization technique that solves problems by breaking them into smaller overlapping subproblems and storing their results.

content.content: DP is applicable when a problem exhibits Overlapping Subproblems and Optimal Substructure.

items.question: Overlapping Subproblems
items.answer: The same subproblems are solved multiple times.

items.question: Optimal Substructure
items.answer: An optimal solution can be built from optimal solutions of smaller subproblems.

content.content: The Fibonacci Problem
The Fibonacci sequence is one of the most common examples used to understand Dynamic Programming.

content.title: Problem with Recursion
content.content: Notice that F(3) and F(2) are calculated multiple times. This repetition causes inefficiency.
Memoization (Top-Down DP)

content.definition: A top-down DP approach where recursion is used and previously computed results are stored in a cache.

content.content: Memoization starts from the original problem and recursively solves smaller subproblems. Whenever a result is computed, it is stored so future calls can reuse it.

content.title: Memoization Example
content.code: int fib(int n, int[] dp){ if(n<=1) return n; if(dp[n]!=-1) return dp[n]; return dp[n]=fib(n-1,dp)+fib(n-2,dp); }

content.content: Advantages of Memoization

items.question: Easy Conversion
items.answer: Recursive solutions can be converted into DP easily.

content.content: Tabulation (Bottom-Up DP)

content.definition: A bottom-up DP approach where smaller subproblems are solved first and used to build larger solutions.

content.content: Tabulation eliminates recursion entirely. Instead, a table is filled from the smallest subproblems up to the final answer.

content.title: Tabulation Example
content.code: int[] dp = new int[n+1]; dp[0]=0; dp[1]=1; for(int i=2;i<=n;i++){ dp[i]=dp[i-1]+dp[i-2]; }

content.content: Memoization vs Tabulation
Space Optimization
Many DP problems only require a few previous states. Instead of storing the entire table, we can store only necessary values.
Common DP Problem Patterns

items.question: Climbing Stairs
items.answer: Count ways to reach the top.

items.question: House Robber
items.answer: Choose non-adjacent houses for maximum profit.

items.question: Coin Change
items.answer: Find minimum coins or total combinations.

content.content: Most interviewers expect candidates to first derive the recursive solution and then optimize it using Dynamic Programming.

content.title: Common Mistake
content.content: Many learners memorize DP solutions without understanding the recurrence relation. Always focus on deriving the state transition first.

content.title: Interview Insight
content.description: Whenever you notice repeated recursive calls solving the same subproblem, think about Dynamic Programming and consider Memoization or Tabulation.

content.title: Quick Revision
points: Dynamic Programming stores results of subproblems.
Space optimization can reduce memory usage.
Fibonacci is the classic DP example.
